imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: The Same Person, Beginning Again. Cast/design continuity: A fictional woman with wavy dark shoulder-length hair, muted rose cardigan, practical dark skirt and flat shoes. Consistent face and body across financial papers at home, wet stone outdoors, and a school approach. A plain cane remains after injury. An immaculate doctor appears only as a faint separate thought image early on, never a literal second person.. CELL 0: Wide modest home study. The real woman sits amid a few unmarked financial papers, shoulders slumped. On the empty wall beyond her is a faint clean white-coat silhouette of an imagined ideal doctor, clearly separate and translucent. She looks toward it without becoming it; hands rest naturally on paper. CELL 1: Wide quiet outdoor path after rain. Same woman in unchanged clothes steps onto a slick stone, foot beginning one small slip as she reaches for balance. Show coherent leg anatomy and a reachable support surface, not a fall from height or prolonged injury spectacle. Soft grey daylight. CELL 2: She sits safely on a low stone edge after the slip, one hand lightly supporting her ankle and the other bracing her weight on the stone. Her face shows ordinary pain and disappointment. The imagined ideal is absent; no miraculous cure, graphic injury or collapse is added. CELL 3: Back in her modest home, same recognizable woman seated at a desk, cane leaning within reach against the chair. She pulls a plain study book toward her with one hand while the other steadies its edge. The financial papers remain a small real stack, not magically vanished. CELL 4: Same desk and woman, reading a study book with pencil contacting a notebook, grounded feet and careful posture. Cane remains clearly beside the chair. Her expression is focused and modestly steadier; no white-coat makeover, diploma or altered body signals success. CELL 5: Wide school approach. The woman stands carefully using the cane in one hand and carrying her study book in the other, taking one slow balanced step toward the entrance. Her face, cardigan, hair and body remain unchanged; the cane is visible and weight bearing, not discarded. Editorial limit: Do not equate starting over with replacing her identity, make over her body or remove the mobility aid. Keep injury modest and real.
